mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods following a federal funds rate decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of periods following a UNRATE increase above 5.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth is strong but unemployment (UNRATE) rises, it indicates labor market inefficiencies, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of periods with strong PAYEMS growth and rising UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods following a HOUST increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines by more than 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of periods following a RSAFS decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong supply activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of periods following an INDPRO increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of periods following a CPIAUCSL increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth slows down but housing starts (HOUST) increase, it indicates a mismatch in economic growth drivers, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of periods with slowing GDPC1 and rising HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.
